content:
You draft referral notes that a primary care provider (PCP) sends to a specialist. The PCP will review, edit and sign your draft, so write it in the PCP's voice, ready to send.

The reader is a specialist who has never met this patient and is triaging many referrals. They need to know quickly why the patient is being sent now, what question the PCP wants answered, what has already been tried or worked up, and anything that would change how they manage the patient. Lead with that. Leave out chart content this specialist has no use for.

Your source is a structured chart extract plus whatever the PCP typed, including their answers to follow-up questions. Every clinical statement in the note must come from one of those. The extract has no free-text notes, so symptoms, examination findings, functional status and patient preferences are absent unless the PCP supplied them; do not supply them yourself. When something this specialist would expect is missing, a follow-up question was left unanswered, or two entries in the chart disagree, say so in the final section so the PCP can fill it in before sending. A note that reads complete but contains an invented detail is worse than one with a visible gap.

Give dates for results and events. For a trend, state the direction with the first and latest values and their dates rather than listing every reading.

Format: plain text with no markdown, because the draft goes into an editable text field. Put each section heading in capitals on its own line, in this order:

REASON FOR REFERRAL
CLINICAL QUESTION
RELEVANT HISTORY
CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
KEY RESULTS
WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING

If the PCP gave no clinical question, propose the one the data best supports and mark it "[suggested - confirm]". Aim for one page, roughly 250 to 400 words. Start directly with the first heading; do not add a greeting, sign-off or commentary about the draft.

<referral_request>
Referring to: Cardiology
Referral condition: Ischemic heart disease / chronic heart failure
Urgency: routine
PCP's clinical question: What lipid-lowering treatment do you recommend given statin intolerance?
PCP's additional notes: Reason for referral now: she stopped taking simvastatin about four months ago because of muscle aches and does not want to restart it. No chest pain since her stent.
</referral_request>

<what_this_specialist_needs>
The cardiologist will want: the cardiac diagnoses with dates, prior events and interventions (MI, PCI, CABG, heart failure admissions), latest ejection fraction and cardiac imaging, current cardiac medications (antiplatelet, statin, beta blocker, ACE inhibitor/ARB, diuretic) and obvious gaps in them, blood pressure and heart rate, lipid and glycemic control, renal function and potassium, recent emergency or inpatient encounters, and smoking status.
</what_this_specialist_needs>

<chart_extract>

Write the referral note.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Ms Justine Murphy is a 55-year-old woman with ischemic heart disease treated with PCI on 2023-09-12. She stopped simvastatin about four months ago because of muscle aches and does not want to restart it. She has had no chest pain since her stent. I would be grateful for your advice on lipid-lowering treatment. This is a routine referral.

CLINICAL QUESTION
What lipid-lowering treatment do you recommend given statin intolerance?

RELEVANT HISTORY
Ischemic heart disease first recorded 2023-08-23. Cardiology referral 2023-08-30 to 2023-09-05, coronary angiography 2023-09-05, PCI 2023-09-12. No emergency, inpatient or urgent care encounters in the last 24 months. Never smoked tobacco (2026-09-09).

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
- Metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg tablet
- Clopidogrel 75 mg tablet
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg/actuation mucosal spray
- Acetaminophen 300 mg / hydrocodone 5 mg tablet (since 2026-09-09)
- Simvastatin 20 mg (stopped about four months ago; still shows as active)
No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- LDL 139.5 mg/dL, total cholesterol 194.9, HDL 30.5, triglycerides 124.6 (all 2025-09-03). LDL was 133.7 on 2022-08-17. No lipid panel since.
- HbA1c 6.2% (2026-09-09), 5.9% (2026-02-18).
- Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (2026-09-09), 1.3 (2026-02-18), 0.8 (2025-09-03).
- Potassium 5.2 mmol/L (2026-09-09), 4.9 (2026-02-18).
- BP 100/71 mmHg and HR 94/min (2026-09-09). Systolic was 119 on 2023-08-23.
- Ejection fraction and cardiac imaging: none in the record.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
Simvastatin 20 mg from 2023-08-30, stopped for muscle aches as above. No other lipid-lowering agent is recorded. No ACE inhibitor, ARB, diuretic or other heart failure therapy is recorded.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
Prediabetes (on a self-management plan), obesity, chronic neck pain, chronic pain, loss of teeth.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
1. The referral condition says chronic heart failure, but no heart failure diagnosis, echo or EF is in the record. Confirm whether to keep this.
2. Update the simvastatin entry to stopped, with the date.
3. Describe the statin intolerance: symptoms, CK, and any other statins or doses tried.
4. Add the most recent echo, angiography findings and stent details, if available.
5. Record prior MI or CABG status.
6. Last lipids were 2025-09-03, before simvastatin stopped. Consider repeating them.
7. Creatinine has risen to 1.3 and potassium is 5.2. Confirm whether these have been repeated or acted on.
8. Confirm whether the absence of ACE inhibitor/ARB and diuretic is intentional.
9. Add current symptoms other than chest pain, such as breathlessness or oedema.
10. BMI is 28.7 on the latest reading, but the findings list says "BMI 30+ obesity". Check which is current.
